title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages. L is a totally ordered set (an abstract 'line'). M is its combinatorial cell structure: points P_a (a in L) and segments S_ab (a<b). M_0 denotes the points and M_1 the segments. The face order ≤ on M has P_a < S_ab and P_b < S_ab. A polyfigure Φ ⊂ M is a set of cells with non-overlapping interiors; its closure F is the figure it generates.

The previous page defines three vertex sets:
- δΦ = F ∩ M_0, the vertices of the closure.
- For convex Φ, ∂Φ is the pair of extremities of the flag δΦ (empty if card δΦ ≤ 1).
- For convex Φ, Φ^· equals ∂Φ, or {a} if Φ = {P_a}, or ∅ if Φ = ∅.
For general Φ, ∂ and ^· are taken as unions over the convex components.

This page:
(1) Example 3. Take Φ = {S_ab, P_b, S_bc, P_d} with a<b<c<d. Its convex components are {S_ab, P_b, S_bc} and {P_d}. Then δΦ = {a,b,c,d}, ∂Φ = {a,c} and Φ^· = {a,c,d}, so the three sets are pairwise different. In the previous page's example, where P_b is missing, b was a boundary point. Here b is interior.
(2) General inclusions: ∂Φ ⊂ Φ^· ⊂ δΦ, canonically.
(3) Intrinsic, local characterisation of the boundary, without passing through convex components: a ∈ ∂Φ iff a ∈ δΦ, some X ∈ Φ has P_a < X, and, when P_a ∈ Φ, that X is unique. A marginal NB adds that if P_a ∈ Φ there are at most two such X (one segment on each side). This is a 'local degree' criterion matching the 'ordre_a' count sketched on the previous page: degree 0 means isolated or exterior, 1 means boundary, 2 means interior. So ∂Φ is the set of non-isolated vertices that are not 'interior'. Also Φ^· = ∂Φ ⊔ Φ_isol, with Φ_isol the isolated components (isolated points).
(4) A second order on M, the positional order <_pos ('X lies to the left of Y'):
- P_x <_pos P_y if x<y;
- P_x <_pos S_ab if x ≤ a;
- S_ab <_pos P_y if b ≤ y;
- S_ab <_pos S_a'b' if b ≤ a'.
It is characterised as: X <_pos Y iff X |·| Y (interiors disjoint, 'disposition' relation) and or(δX) < ex(δY), i.e. smallest vertex of X < largest vertex of Y. The next page uses this to show that |·| is exactly the comparability relation of <_pos. It then extends <_pos to sets of cells and refines it to a strict version that forbids a shared endpoint P_a, in preparation for concatenation/juxtaposition of admissible polyfigures.

Overall purpose: set up a purely combinatorial, order-theoretic 1-dimensional 'analysis situs' (tame topology of the line). The notions in play are figures, their vertices, boundary and isolated points, and a left/right positional order needed later to glue figures.
errors: The characterisation of ∂Φ and the 'at most two X' remark need Φ to be a genuine polyfigure (segments with disjoint interiors). For arbitrary subsets of M, e.g. {P_a, S_ab, S_ac}, it fails. Grothendieck's own marginal caveat '(s'il y a plus grand ou plus petit élément dans L!)' signals a further boundary-case subtlety that is left unresolved on the page.
Otherwise the computations are correct. Example 3 checks out, and <_pos is irreflexive and transitive. The equivalence X <_pos Y ⟺ X|·|Y and or(δX) < ex(δY) checks out in all four cases.

ideas.what: Vertex set δ, boundary ∂ and 'boundary plus isolated points' Φ^· of a finite cell configuration on an ordered line, with ∂ ⊂ Φ^· ⊂ δ and boundary characterised by local valence (number of incident segments = 1, or vertex not in Φ but incident to a segment)
ideas.modern_name: boundary of a 1-dimensional cell complex / chain via local degree (mod-2 boundary of a 1-chain, valence of vertices in a graph)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard combinatorial topology (Poincaré; simplicial homology folklore)

ideas.what: Positional order <_pos on points and segments of a line ('X entirely to the left of Y, touching allowed at endpoints'), whose comparability relation is disjointness of interiors
ideas.modern_name: interval order on relatively open cells (Fishburn interval orders); left-of order in o-minimal / tame cell decompositions of the line
ideas.usually_credited_to: Wiener (1914), Fishburn (1970) for interval orders; van den Dries for o-minimal cell decompositions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) calls for a 'topologie modérée' but does not contain this formalism

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary bookkeeping for a combinatorial model of tame topology in dimension one: boundaries of polyfigures and a positional (interval-type) order. It is historically interesting as a trace of the 1986 'analysis situs' project following the Esquisse's call for tame topology, but contains no result unknown to specialists.
transcription_corrections: '∃ X ∈ Φ quand P_a < X' should read '∃ X ∈ Φ tel que P_a < X'.
'X ‖ Y [?]' should be 'X |·| Y' (the disposition / non-crossing relation used on the next page).
'ens. des composantes non isolées de Φ' should probably be 'ens. des sommets non isolés de Φ qui … ne sont pas « intérieurs » à Φ'.
In 'Φ_isol est l'ens. des … isolés de Φ' the crossed-out word is 'points', replaced by 'composants' (isolated components).
The interlinear insertion above the ∂Φ characterisation reads '(s'il y a plus grand ou plus petit élément dans L!)'.
Under 'or(δX) < ex(δY)' the glosses are 'plus petit élément de δX' and 'plus grand él. de δY'.
